features.name: hard_delete_audit_all_modules
features.title: Remove unsafe hard-delete endpoints across the API and standardize on soft-delete
features.description: Surfaced by testing_integration_api and confirmed by a cross-module audit: the same swallowing-catch + missing-cascade bug exists in 4 modules — organizations, customers, customer-assets, services. Rather than fix each one with cascade rules and 409 semantics (which preserves an unsafe surface), this feature removes the hard-delete capability outright. Rationale: customers and customer-assets have legal/fiscal retention requirements (invoices reference them for 5+ years); services already expose explicit activate/deactivate semantics that supersede hard-delete; organizations' permanent-delete has no UI caller and no proven product use case (Testcontainers handles test cleanup). Soft-delete (status=DELETED, or isActive=false for services) becomes the single deletion path. If GDPR or tenant-decommissioning needs hard-delete in the future, those flows get a dedicated design with explicit retention rules, not a query-param toggle. Spec at openspec/changes/hard-delete-audit-all-modules/.
acceptance: Audit data captured in design.md: the 4 affected modules (organizations, customers, customer-assets, services) are listed with their swallowing-catch line ranges. The other 12 modules are documented as CASCADE_SAFE, SOFT_ONLY, or FINANCIAL with one-line reasoning
permanent query parameter removed from controllers and DTOs in organizations, customers, customer-assets. DELETE endpoints always do soft-delete (status=DELETED)
DELETE /services/:id endpoint removed entirely; consumers use POST /services/:id/deactivate (already exists)

All four service methods drop the broad try { delete } catch { throw NotFoundException } block. removeOrganization, removeCustomer, removeCustomerAsset, removeService no longer call prisma.X.delete() — they only soft-delete or no-op
Hard-delete repository methods (.delete(id)) in the 4 affected modules are removed unless still used internally (e.g., by tests). If kept, they are isolated and documented
Existing e2e scenarios that exercised permanent=true are removed; new scenarios assert that DELETE still soft-deletes and that the permanent flag (if sent) is ignored or rejected with 400
Unit tests for the 4 services drop the cascade-path tests and keep the soft-delete-path tests. New tests confirm permanent=true does not bypass soft-delete
Existing soft-delete behavior is unchanged for callers — DELETE without permanent still returns the same status and result
No Prisma migration is required (we are removing code paths, not changing schema). Cascade rules stay default — there are no hard-deletes that would trigger them
pnpm --filter api test (601 tests) and pnpm --filter api test:e2e (94 tests) both pass; ./init.sh green

features.name: shared_request_schemas_zod_migration
features.title: Migrate API request validation to Zod via ZodValidationPipe and publish request schemas in @glossops/shared
features.description: Surfaced while reviewing the shared schemas alignment: today there is duplication between the API DTOs (class-validator, 49 files under apps/api/src/<module>/dto/) and the web form schemas (Zod, 7 files in apps/web/src/lib/schemas/). The two sides describe the same request shape with different tools and drift over time. This feature replaces class-validator in apps/api with a custom ZodValidationPipe, publishes every request schema in @glossops/shared as a single source of truth, and points both apps/api and apps/web at the published schemas. Depends on (and should land after) feat 33 to start from a clean Zod foundation in shared.
acceptance: ZodValidationPipe implemented in apps/api/src/common (or equivalent) and wired as a global pipe in main.ts, replacing the class-validator ValidationPipe
Every request body, query, and route param across all 16 modules is validated via a Zod schema imported from @glossops/shared
All 49 class-validator DTOs under apps/api/src/<module>/dto/ are deleted; their Zod replacements live in @glossops/shared/request-schemas (or equivalent namespace)
All 7 form schemas under apps/web/src/lib/schemas/ are deleted; apps/web imports the request schemas from @glossops/shared and derives form value types via z.infer
Partial updates (PATCH endpoints) are typed via .partial() on the create schema where applicable
OpenAPI/Swagger metadata is preserved (either via the chosen Zod-to-OpenAPI integration or hand-authored decorators on the pipe layer)
All existing unit tests (currently 601 across 54 suites) continue to pass
All integration tests (17 suites / 94 tests after feat 33) continue to pass
apps/web typecheck stays green and existing form behavior (validation errors, defaults, transformations) is preserved
pnpm --filter api lint and pnpm --filter web lint both pass
class-validator and class-transformer are removed from apps/api dependencies
